Title: Might of the camarilla burned from play?

Messages.Author: d-mohn
Messages.Body:
is a vampire burned by the effect of the political action might of the camarilla considered burned from play for the purposes of playing blessed resilience?

Might of the Camarilla
Type
Political Action
Card Text
Requires a justicar or Inner Circle member. If this referendum is successful, each Methuselah burns a vampire (of his or her choosing) in his or her uncontrolled region.

Blessed Resilience
Type
Master
Card Text
Move a vampire in your ash heap with superior Fortitude [FOR] and superior Necromancy [NEC] who was burned from play to your ready region (with no blood).

Messages.Author: lip
Messages.Body:
I would say yes, since the uncontrolled region is part of the Play Area. See Rulebook www.vekn.net/rulebook#play-area :
>
> Play Area
> The area in front of each Methuselah is divided into two regions: the uncontrolled region (6), and the controlled region (7).
>
But I must say this looks counter-intuitive to me

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
I would say no based on the Targeting of Cards rule stating that cards which aren´t controlled are not considered in play.
See Rulebook www.vekn.net/rulebook#targeting-of-cards :
>
> Targeting of Cards
> If a card is played on another card, or targets another card, the target card must be in play (that is, controlled). Vampires in the torpor region are eligible targets by default, but vampires in the uncontrolled region and contested cards are not.
>

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> d-mohn wrote:
> is a vampire burned by the effect of the political action might of the camarilla considered burned from play for the purposes of playing blessed resilience?
>
No. As inm8 quoted the rulebook, burned from play means the vampire was controlled when it was burned.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Legion
Messages.Body:
What happen with cards burned with Might of the Camarilla?
Are they moved to ash heap or removed from the game?

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
As per the rules burned cards go to the discard pile aka ash heap.
See rulebook ​​​​​​​www.vekn.net/rulebook#burn
>
> Burn
> When a card is burned, it is placed into its owner’s ash heap (discard pile).
>

Messages.Author: Legion
Messages.Body: But that means cards in the ash heap have to remember their previous state in a purpose of playing Blessed Resilience... I don't think it makes sense.

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body: Agree with you that it isn´t very practical ....i assume it was put in as part of the requirement to not get some undesired combos to work that could result in getting a lot of vampires into play for close to no pool cost.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
> Legion wrote:
> But that means cards in the ash heap have to remember their previous state in a purpose of playing Blessed Resilience... I don't think it makes sense.
>
Very few things in VTES rules make sense, but thats the way it is.

For example, Toreador grand ball is not actually placed on any vampire, but you have to remember two different vampires in two different states (one to that doesnt unlock and one that is unblockable) regardless, with nothing in particular to help track them. It is also very logical that one vampire can dance with two others, and that they can dance while torporized, isn't it?

This is a game from the nineties that hasn't evolved, and it shows.

Smoking craters tell no tales.
